author: agent:claude-code
rationale: The user asked for the Windows folder layout (vg-workspace/studio/documents/library/tools, school/work/projects, vg-wallpapers) on every Nix archetype, in the home folder; vgwsl2 KVM for NixOS VM tests (user in kvm, Windows side asked by graft)

ops.name: folders
ops.intent: The user-data folders every machine shares with vg-dotfiles-windows, in the home directory (~/vg-workspace with projects, school and work; ~/vg-studio; ~/vg-documents; ~/vg-library; ~/vg-tools), and the private vg-wallpapers repo cloned into ~/Pictures on machines with a desktop.

ops.text: The ~/vg-* tree mirrors vg-dotfiles-windows' C:\vg-* folders, in the home directory on every Nix archetype
ops.why: The user wants one layout across Windows, NixOS, NixOS-WSL and macOS, kept in the home folder here rather than at the root. The list matches home.psd1's `folders` (vg-dotfiles-windows), relative to the home directory, and is created by a home-manager activation step (mkdir -p, so idempotent and the same on macOS, where tmpfiles doesn't exist). Applied on vgwsl2: all 13 folders created.

ops.text: vg-wallpapers is cloned once over HTTPS and never pulled by a rebuild; a clone that can't happen warns
ops.why: Same contract as Windows: the repo is private, so HTTPS through gh's git credential helper clones it before a machine has an SSH key; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes a missing login fail in about a second instead of hanging activation, and the rebuild warns and carries on (checked on vgwsl2 without gh login). New images come from `git pull` there. Off by default on headless hosts (nixtype.headless) and NixOS-WSL, which have no desktop. The successful clone isn't tested yet (no gh login on vgwsl2); the slideshow itself is graft 01a165aa from vg-dotfiles-windows, still open.

ops.text: vgwsl2 runs NixOS VM tests on KVM once Windows exposes AMD-V
ops.why: Other projects' `nix flake check` (Jacquard's VM tests) should run locally. The user is in the kvm group; Nix's system-features already include kvm and nixos-test (the NixOS default). WSL ships kvm-amd as a module (CONFIG_KVM_AMD=m, in /lib/modules), but after a WSL restart with nestedVirtualization=true the guest still had no svm flag and `Hyper-V: Nested features: 0x0` (VBS running), so the Windows side is asked by graft 01a165ae-63a0 (vg-dotfiles-windows).

ops.title: vgwsl2: check /dev/kvm once Windows exposes AMD-V; load kvm-amd only if it's still missing
ops.body: After the Windows fix and a WSL restart: grep -c svm /proc/cpuinfo > 0; ls -l /dev/kvm (group kvm, 0660); if missing, try `modprobe kvm_amd` first, then declare boot.kernelModules = [ "kvm-amd" ] only if that's what makes it appear (WSL uses Microsoft's kernel). Then run a NixOS VM test to confirm.
